snippet.description:
In the heart of WWII Shanghai, diabetic refugee Eva Saxl faced an unimaginable crisis—her insulin supply ran out, and with it, her hope for survival. Refusing to give up, Eva and her husband Victor took matters into their own hands, crafting insulin from water buffalo pancreases in a makeshift lab. After months of painstaking experiments and tests on rabbits, Eva bravely injected herself with the homemade insulin. Against all odds, it worked. This life-saving discovery didn't just rescue Eva; it saved over 200 others in the Shanghai ghetto. A story of courage, innovation, and resilience, Eva Saxl's journey is a testament to the power of human determination.
